description_good_justification: The README opens with what speccer does: it annotates or highlights HTML elements on a web page, for documenting components in a design system: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/blob/main/README.md#about
interact_justification: speccer.dev explains how to install and use speccer (https://speccer.dev/guide/introduction/), and its development page (https://speccer.dev/guide/development) links to CONTRIBUTING.md, which explains how to report bugs and suggest enhancements on GitHub: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#reporting-bugs
contribution_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md explains how to report bugs, suggest enhancements and contribute code: the development commands, coding style, tests, DCO sign-off, commits and pull requests, and the checks every pull request must pass: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#contributing-code
contribution_requirements_justification: The development guide gives the coding standard (ESLint and Prettier, npm run style:lint) and the commit style (conventional commits with npm run commit): https://speccer.dev/guide/development#clean-code
documentation_basics_justification: Installation, usage with ES modules, CommonJS, a script tag and React, and every feature, on speccer.dev: https://speccer.dev/guide/introduction/
documentation_interface_justification: The API reference, generated from the source with TypeDoc and checked in CI with warnings as errors: https://speccer.dev/api/
sites_https_justification: speccer.dev (HTTPS enforced on GitHub Pages), the repository and the npm package are all served over HTTPS: https://speccer.dev/
discussion_justification: GitHub issues and pull requests are searchable, addressable by URL and open to anyone with a GitHub account: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/issues
english_justification: All documentation is in English, and reports and comments in English are accepted.
maintained_justification: The project is actively maintained, with releases 11.4.2 to 11.4.6 in October 2026 and changes since: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/releases
repo_track_justification: Git records who changed what and when: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/commits/main
repo_interim_justification: Every change is a public commit and pull request between releases, not only the releases themselves.
version_unique_justification: Every release has a unique version, tagged as v<version>: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/tags
version_semver_justification: Semantic Versioning; the public API only breaks in a major release: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/blob/main/SECURITY.md#supported-versions
version_tags_justification: Each release is tagged in git as v<version>: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/tags
release_notes_justification: A CHANGELOG.md generated from conventional commits, also published as GitHub release notes: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md
release_notes_vulns_justification: No release has fixed a vulnerability that had a CVE or advisory. The one security fix so far, inserting values read from the page as text instead of HTML (https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/issues/487), is listed in the 11.4.2 release notes: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/releases/tag/v11.4.2
report_tracker_justification: Issues are tracked on GitHub: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/issues
report_responses_justification: Every issue is assigned to the maintainer when it is opened. No one outside the project has filed a bug report in the last 12 months, so none is unanswered.
enhancement_responses_justification: Enhancement requests are answered in their GitHub issue. No one outside the project has filed one in the last 12 months, so none is unanswered.
report_archive_justification: All issues and pull requests stay public and searchable on GitHub: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/issues?q=is%3Aissue
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: Private reports through GitHub private vulnerability reporting or by email: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/blob/main/SECURITY.md#reporting-a-vulnerability
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: Reports are acknowledged within 7 days; no vulnerability has been reported in the last 6 months: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/blob/main/SECURITY.md#how-reports-are-handled
build_justification: npm run build builds the ES module, CommonJS and UMD builds and the type declarations with rollup, and the stylesheets with Stylus and PostCSS: https://speccer.dev/guide/development
build_common_tools_justification: npm, rollup, the TypeScript compiler, Stylus and PostCSS.
build_floss_tools_justification: npm, Node.js, rollup, TypeScript, Stylus and PostCSS are all FLOSS.
test_justification: A node:test suite run with npm test, Playwright end-to-end tests of every feature in Chromium and Firefox (npm run test:e2e), and a packaging check (npm run check:pack) that installs the packed package and loads it from every entry point: https://speccer.dev/guide/development
test_invocation_justification: npm test, the standard way to run tests in an npm project.
test_most_justification: The unit tests cover 94% of lines, 88% of branches and 97% of functions of the source, and test:ci fails below 82% of lines, 85% of branches or 88% of functions; the end-to-end tests exercise every feature in two browsers. Coverage is uploaded to Codecov from every CI run.
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: The CI workflow lints, type-checks, tests, builds, packs and checks the docs on every pull request and every push to main: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml
test_policy_justification: New functionality must come with tests, and bug fixes with a regression test that fails without the fix: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#tests
tests_are_added_justification: Recent changes came with tests: the fix for https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/issues/487 in 11.4.2 came with unit tests and an end-to-end test that loads markup and script payloads into every annotation: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/blob/main/tests/e2e/untrusted-content.e2e.ts
tests_documented_added_justification: The test policy is written down in CONTRIBUTING.md: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#tests
warnings_justification: ESLint (typescript-eslint, import and Prettier rules) runs on every file, Markdown included, the TypeScript compiler type-checks the source and the tests, and TypeDoc treats warnings as errors.
warnings_fixed_justification: Lint has no errors and no warnings, TypeScript has no errors, and TypeDoc has no warnings.
warnings_strict_justification: TypeScript runs with strict: true and noImplicitReturns for the source and the tests, ESLint fails CI on any warning (--max-warnings 0), and TypeDoc treats warnings as errors: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/blob/main/tsconfig.build.json
know_secure_design_justification: The maintainer knows how to design secure software. The principles applied: no runtime dependencies, no network, storage or dynamic code, values read from the page inserted as text, least-privilege CI tokens, pinned Actions, and releases with provenance. What speccer guarantees and does not: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/blob/main/SECURITY.md#security-expectations
know_common_errors_justification: The maintainer knows the common errors for this kind of software: cross-site scripting through values read from the page (escaped before they are inserted, and tested with payloads in two browsers), dynamic code (none), and the supply chain (no runtime dependencies, checked in CI, locked and reviewed development dependencies, pinned Actions): https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/blob/main/SECURITY.md#security-expectations
crypto_published_justification: speccer implements and calls no cryptography and makes no network requests: it reads elements in the page and adds annotation elements to it. Annotation ids come from Math.random(), which is not used for anything security-related. See the security expectations: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/blob/main/SECURITY.md#security-expectations

delivery_mitm_justification: The package is delivered by npm over HTTPS with Sigstore-signed provenance, the repository by GitHub over HTTPS, and the documentation from speccer.dev over HTTPS.
delivery_unsigned_justification: No hashes are fetched over HTTP; npm verifies package integrity from the registry metadata over HTTPS.
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: The published package has no dependencies and no known vulnerabilities (npm audit --omit=dev runs before every release). The one security issue found in speccer itself, https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/issues/487, was fixed within 17 days. Development tooling alerts are fixed or accepted as described in the security policy: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/blob/main/SECURITY.md#dependencies
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: No critical vulnerability has been found in the published package.
no_leaked_credentials_justification: No credentials are in the repository or its history; GitHub secret scanning with push protection is enabled: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/blob/main/SECURITY.md#secrets
static_analysis_justification: CodeQL (GitHub default setup) analyses every pull request and push to main, and ESLint runs on every pull request.
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: CodeQL analyses the JavaScript/TypeScript code and the GitHub Actions workflows on every push to main and every pull request, and the ruleset on main requires its results, with no errors and no high or critical security alerts, before merging: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/blob/main/SECURITY.md#code-scanning
static_analysis_fixed_justification: CodeQL has no open alerts; the ruleset blocks merging with a high or critical one.
static_analysis_often_justification: On every pull request and every push to main.
dynamic_analysis_justification: The unit tests are an automated test suite with at least 80% branch coverage: test:ci fails below 85% of branches. They run in the CI workflow on every pull request, and main only accepts pull requests that pass it, so every release has been through them. The end-to-end tests also run every feature in Chromium and Firefox, including markup and script payloads: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: All software is TypeScript on JavaScript runtimes, which are memory-safe; there is no C, C++ or other memory-unsafe code.
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: No run-time assertions beyond the argument checks: since 11.6.0 the public functions throw a TypeError when given something that isn't an element, and the tests run with those checks.
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: The test suite has found no medium or higher severity vulnerabilities. One found by it is handled like a report, with a fix aimed for within 30 days: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/blob/main/SECURITY.md#how-reports-are-handled
achieve_passing_justification: The project has the passing badge: https://www.bestpractices.dev/projects/16759
dco_justification: Every commit must be signed off under the Developer Certificate of Origin, checked on every pull request by the DCO app and required by the ruleset on main: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#developer-certificate-of-origin
governance_justification: The maintainer-led governance model and how decisions are made: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md
roles_responsibilities_justification: The maintainer and contributor roles and their responsibilities, and who holds them: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#roles
access_continuity_justification: One maintainer holds the access to the repository, the npm package and the speccer.dev domain today. Releases use npm trusted publishing (no personal token) and the code is MIT-licensed, but no second person holds access yet: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#continuity
bus_factor_justification: The project has one maintainer, so the bus factor is 1: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/graphs/contributors
documentation_roadmap_justification: What the project plans to do and not do from November 2026 to November 2027, linking the issues: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/blob/main/ROADMAP.md
documentation_architecture_justification: The source, the features, the builds (ES module, CommonJS, UMD, types and CSS), the checks and the docs site: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#architecture
documentation_security_justification: What users can and cannot rely on: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/blob/main/SECURITY.md#security-expectations
documentation_quick_start_justification: Installation and quick usage with a script tag and with an import: https://speccer.dev/guide/introduction/
documentation_current_justification: The API reference is generated from the source with TypeDoc, CI fails on TypeDoc warnings, and every release regenerates docs/api. CI also builds speccer.dev and checks every page for broken links and anchors (npm run check:site), and checks that every file and heading linked from .bestpractices.json and security-insights.yml exists. Documentation defects are fixed as normal changes.
documentation_achievements_justification: The README shows the OpenSSF Best Practices and Scorecard badges: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/blob/main/README.md
accessibility_best_practices_justificati: speccer.dev is checked in CI on every page with axe (WCAG 2.0, 2.1 and 2.2 A and AA) in light and dark, and for horizontal scroll at 390, 768 and 1440 pixels wide: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/blob/main/scripts/check-site.mjs . The a11y feature itself documents tab stops, landmarks, headings, shortcuts and autocomplete. The annotations are not hidden from assistive technology, which the assurance case lists as a known gap: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/blob/main/ASSURANCE.md#known-gaps
internationalization_justification: The package shows no prose of its own: annotations show values read from the page, CSS values, element names and measurements, and pin text comes from the page's own attributes, in its own language. Its only own text is error messages for developers.
sites_password_security_justification: The project sites (GitHub, npm and the static speccer.dev site) store no passwords for external users.
maintenance_or_update_justification: The current major is supported as a whole, and the previous one gets high and critical security fixes for 6 months after the next major. Breaking changes come only in a major, each with a BREAKING CHANGE note in the release notes that says what to change: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/blob/main/SECURITY.md#supported-versions
vulnerability_report_credit_justificatio: No one outside the project has reported a vulnerability in the last 12 months; the repository has no security advisories. The one security fix, https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/issues/487 , was found by the maintainer.
vulnerability_response_process_justifica: Reports are made privately through GitHub private vulnerability reporting or by email. Acknowledgement within 7 days, assessment, a fix in a private GitHub security advisory, disclosure with the release, and credit: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/blob/main/SECURITY.md#how-reports-are-handled
coding_standards_justification: Code follows the project ESLint configuration (eslint-config-phun-ky) and Prettier, type-checks with TypeScript in strict mode, and must pass npm run style:lint, npx tsc and npm run docs:check: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#coding-style
coding_standards_enforced_justification: The CI workflow runs ESLint (with Prettier) with no warnings allowed, the TypeScript compiler in strict mode and TypeDoc with warnings as errors on every pull request, and the ruleset on main requires its check job to pass before merging: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml
build_standard_variables_justification: No native binaries are built; rollup, TypeScript, Stylus and PostCSS compile TypeScript and Stylus to JavaScript and CSS.
build_preserve_debug_justification: The published builds are minified with terser and ship without source maps (sourcemap: false in rollup.config.js), and the build has no option to keep them. The TypeScript source of every release is in the repository at its tag.
build_non_recursive_justification: npm run build runs rollup once (the JavaScript builds, then the types), then Stylus and PostCSS, in sequence; nothing builds recursively.
build_repeatable_justification: Dependencies are locked in package-lock.json and installed with npm ci. Rebuilding tag v11.9.0 and packing it gave a package identical, file by file, to the published 11.9.0 tarball.
installation_common_justification: The package is installed and removed with npm: npm install @phun-ky/speccer and npm uninstall @phun-ky/speccer.
installation_standard_variables_justific: Installation is done entirely by npm, which honours its standard location settings (--prefix, npm_config_prefix, global or local). The package has no preinstall, install or postinstall scripts.
installation_development_quick_justifica: git clone, npm ci, npm run build and npm test give the full development and test environment: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#development
external_dependencies_justification: The package has no runtime dependencies; development dependencies are listed in package.json and locked in package-lock.json: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/blob/main/package.json
dependency_monitoring_justification: Dependabot checks npm dependencies and GitHub Actions weekly, dependency review checks every pull request, and npm audit runs before every release: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/blob/main/SECURITY.md#dependencies
updateable_reused_components_justificati: No third-party code is copied into the repository; all external components come from npm through package.json and the lockfile, the package has no runtime dependencies to bundle, and Dependabot opens update pull requests.
interfaces_current_justification: The code uses current interfaces: ES modules with an exports map, IntersectionObserver for lazy mode, checkVisibility where the browser has it, Node 24 in CI, TypeScript 6.0 in strict mode, and current GitHub Actions pinned to commit SHAs.
automated_integration_testing_justificat: The CI workflow lints, type-checks, runs the unit tests with coverage, builds, packs and installs the package and loads it from every entry point, runs the Playwright end-to-end tests in Chromium and Firefox, and checks and builds the docs site, on every pull request and push to main, with coverage uploaded to Codecov: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml
regression_tests_added50_justification: 9 of the 12 fix commits since May 2026 came with tests. Of the three others, one changed only the homepage in package.json, and the fix for import and require in Node is checked by npm run check:pack, added the same day.
test_statement_coverage80_justification: Line coverage of the source (tests and types excluded), measured with Node built-in coverage on every CI run and uploaded to Codecov, is 94%. test:ci fails below 82% of lines, 88% of functions or 85% of branches: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#tests
test_policy_mandated_justification: New functionality must come with tests, and bug fixes with a regression test that fails without the fix: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#tests
implement_secure_design_justification: Secure design principles applied (economy of mechanism, fail-safe defaults, least privilege, open design, no dynamic code, no runtime dependencies): https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/blob/main/ASSURANCE.md#secure-design-principles

signed_releases_justification: From 11.3.19 on, releases are published from GitHub Actions with npm trusted publishing and carry a Sigstore-signed SLSA provenance attestation that names the repository, the workflow and the commit, for example 11.9.0: https://registry.npmjs.org/-/npm/v1/attestations/@phun-ky%2fspeccer@11.9.0 . Users verify it with npm audit signatures; the steps are in https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/blob/main/SECURITY.md#verifying-releases . Earlier releases have npm's registry signature but no provenance.
version_tags_signed_justification: Release tags are annotated but not signed; releases are verified through npm provenance instead.
input_validation_justification: Every exported function that takes an element throws a TypeError for anything else. The words in a data-speccer attribute are only compared with fixed lists, so an unknown word changes nothing, and every value read from the page is escaped before it is shown. Checks on the remaining options are planned for 12.0: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/blob/main/ASSURANCE.md#trust-boundaries
hardening_justification: No runtime dependencies, values read from the page escaped before they are inserted, elements checked, no eval or dynamic code, read-only CI permissions with SHA-pinned actions, CodeQL on every change, and npm audit and a pack check before every release: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/blob/main/ASSURANCE.md
assurance_case_justification: What is protected, the threat model, trust boundaries, secure design principles, the common weaknesses countered and the known gaps: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/blob/main/ASSURANCE.md
osps_ac_01_01_justification: The maintainer, the only person with access, uses two-factor authentication on GitHub, which GitHub requires for code contributors. Anyone given access later must use it too: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#becoming-a-maintainer
osps_ac_02_01_justification: GitHub requires a role to be chosen for every collaborator invited to the repository, and the governance requires the lowest role that fits: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#becoming-a-maintainer
osps_ac_03_01_justification: The ruleset on main requires changes to arrive through a pull request with passing checks. Only the maintainer, as administrator, can bypass it, which the release workflow uses to push its commit and tag: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#reviews
osps_ac_03_02_justification: A separate ruleset on main, with no bypass, blocks deleting the branch and force pushes.
osps_br_01_01_justification: No workflow interpolates untrusted metadata, such as pull request titles or branch names, into a script; github.actor and the pull request's commit SHAs are passed through environment variables: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/blob/main/.github/workflows/publish.yml
osps_br_01_03_justification: Pull requests run on the pull_request event, where forks get no secrets. The labeler runs on pull_request_target but never checks out or runs pull request code. Publishing runs only after a merge or when the maintainer starts it, and the docs site deploys only from main.
osps_br_03_01_justification: All official channels use HTTPS: the GitHub repository, the npm package and the docs site at https://speccer.dev/
osps_br_03_02_justification: The package is distributed by npm over HTTPS with a registry signature on every version, and from 11.3.19 on with a Sigstore-signed provenance attestation: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/blob/main/SECURITY.md#verifying-releases
osps_br_07_01_justification: GitHub secret scanning with push protection is enabled and blocks commits that contain secrets; secrets are kept only in GitHub Actions secrets: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/blob/main/SECURITY.md#secrets
osps_do_01_01_justification: Installation, usage and every feature, on speccer.dev: https://speccer.dev/guide/introduction/
osps_do_02_01_justification: How to report a bug, with an issue template: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#reporting-bugs
osps_gv_02_01_justification: Proposed changes and usage problems are discussed in public GitHub issues and pull requests: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/issues
osps_le_02_01_justification: The source code is under the MIT licence, which is OSI-approved: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/blob/main/LICENSE
osps_le_02_02_justification: The released npm package is under the MIT licence, declared in package.json: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/blob/main/LICENSE
osps_le_03_01_justification: The licence is in the LICENSE file at the repository root: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/blob/main/LICENSE
osps_le_03_02_justification: The published package includes the licence text in its LICENSE file, and every build starts with the licence notice: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/blob/main/LICENSE
osps_qa_01_01_justification: The repository is public at https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer
osps_qa_01_02_justification: The full git history, with authors and dates, is public: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/commits/main
osps_qa_02_01_justification: The package has no runtime dependencies; development dependencies are listed in package.json, with every version locked in package-lock.json: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/blob/main/package.json
osps_qa_04_01_justification: The project has a single repository.
osps_qa_05_01_justification: No generated executables are committed: the build output (dist and dts) is ignored, and the package is built in CI.
osps_qa_05_02_justification: The only binary files are the PNG and JPEG images for the README and the docs site, no executables.
osps_vm_02_01_justification: Security contacts (email and GitHub private vulnerability reporting): https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/blob/main/SECURITY.md#reporting-a-vulnerability
osps_ac_04_01_justification: Every workflow sets read-only permissions at the top level, and jobs ask only for what they need: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml
osps_br_02_01_justification: Every release has a unique Semantic Versioning version, tagged as v<version>: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/releases
osps_br_04_01_justification: A CHANGELOG.md generated from conventional commits, listing features, fixes and breaking changes, also published as GitHub release notes: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md
osps_br_05_01_justification: Dependencies are installed with npm ci from the lockfile in every pipeline: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/blob/main/.github/workflows/publish.yml
osps_br_06_01_justification: Every version on npm is accounted for in the registry's signature over its integrity hash, verifiable with npm audit signatures, and from 11.3.19 on also carries a Sigstore-signed provenance attestation: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/blob/main/SECURITY.md#verifying-releases
osps_do_06_01_justification: How dependencies are chosen, obtained, tracked and fixed: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/blob/main/SECURITY.md#dependencies
osps_gv_01_01_justification: Who has access to the repository, the npm package and the speccer.dev domain: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#continuity
osps_gv_01_02_justification: The maintainer and contributor roles and their responsibilities: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#roles
osps_gv_03_02_justification: Requirements for code contributions: architecture, development, coding style, tests, sign-off, commits, pull requests and releases: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#contributing-code
osps_le_01_01_justification: Every commit must carry a Developer Certificate of Origin sign-off, checked on every pull request by the DCO app and required by the ruleset on main: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#developer-certificate-of-origin
osps_qa_03_01_justification: The ruleset on main requires the status checks (check, dependency-review and DCO) and CodeQL results to pass before merging; only an administrator can bypass it: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#reviews
osps_qa_06_01_justification: The CI workflow builds and runs the unit and end-to-end tests, the pack check and the docs checks on every pull request, and must pass before merging: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml
osps_sa_01_01_justification: The architecture (the source, the features, the builds, the checks and the docs site): https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#architecture
osps_sa_02_01_justification: The exported functions, their options, the data-speccer attributes and the types are described in the guide and the generated API reference: https://speccer.dev/api/
osps_sa_03_01_justification: The assurance case assesses the most likely and impactful security problems: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/blob/main/ASSURANCE.md
osps_vm_01_01_justification: Coordinated disclosure, with acknowledgement within 7 days and a fix within 30 days for serious issues: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/blob/main/SECURITY.md#how-reports-are-handled
osps_vm_03_01_justification: Private reporting through GitHub private vulnerability reporting or the security email: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/blob/main/SECURITY.md#reporting-a-vulnerability
osps_vm_04_01_justification: Vulnerabilities are published as GitHub security advisories when the fix is released: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/security/advisories
osps_ac_04_02_justification: Each job declares only the permissions it needs, for example the labeler and auto-assign have issues: write and pull-requests: write, publishing id-token: write, and the docs deploy pages: write and id-token: write: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/blob/main/.github/workflows/publish.yml
osps_br_01_04_justification: Workflows take no manual inputs, and the only collaborator-controlled value used in a script, github.actor, is passed through an environment variable: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/blob/main/.github/workflows/publish.yml
osps_br_02_02_justification: Each release is a versioned npm package and a GitHub release with the same tag, and from 11.4.6 on its SBOM is named speccer-<version>.cdx.json: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/releases
osps_br_07_02_justification: How secrets are stored, accessed and rotated: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/blob/main/SECURITY.md#secrets
osps_do_03_01_justification: How to verify release integrity with npm audit signatures: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/blob/main/SECURITY.md#verifying-releases
osps_do_03_02_justification: How to check that a release was built by the publish workflow in phun-ky/speccer, from its provenance: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/blob/main/SECURITY.md#verifying-releases
osps_do_04_01_justification: The current major (11.x) is supported as a whole; the previous major gets high and critical security fixes for 6 months after the next major is released: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/blob/main/SECURITY.md#supported-versions
osps_do_05_01_justification: A major stops getting security updates 6 months after the next major is released; 10.x and older get none: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/blob/main/SECURITY.md#supported-versions
osps_gv_04_01_justification: Collaborators are reviewed, including two-factor authentication, before getting escalated permissions, such as publishing rights on npm: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#becoming-a-maintainer
osps_qa_02_02_justification: From 11.4.6 on, every GitHub release has a CycloneDX SBOM of the package's runtime dependencies (none today) attached, generated by the publish workflow: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/blob/main/SECURITY.md#verifying-releases
osps_qa_04_02_justification: The project has a single repository, so there are no subprojects in other repositories.
osps_qa_06_02_justification: When and how the tests run, locally and in CI: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#tests
osps_qa_06_03_justification: New functionality and bug fixes must come with tests: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#tests
osps_qa_07_01_justification: The project has one maintainer, so no non-author approval is possible yet. A review by a maintainer other than the author is required once there is a second maintainer: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#reviews
osps_sa_03_02_justification: Threat model, trust boundaries and attack surface: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/blob/main/ASSURANCE.md#threat-model
osps_vm_04_02_justification: Vulnerabilities in dependencies that don't affect the package are recorded as OpenVEX statements: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/blob/main/vex.openvex.json
osps_vm_05_01_justification: Thresholds for fixing vulnerability and licence findings in dependencies: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/blob/main/SECURITY.md#dependencies
osps_vm_05_02_justification: Releases are blocked while a runtime dependency has a known high or critical vulnerability (npm audit in the publish workflow): https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/blob/main/SECURITY.md#dependencies
osps_vm_05_03_justification: Dependency review checks every pull request against the GitHub Advisory Database and blocks high or critical findings, as the documented policy says: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/blob/main/.github/workflows/dependency-review.yml
osps_vm_06_02_justification: The ruleset on main blocks merging while CodeQL reports an error or a high or critical security alert: https://github.com/phun-ky/speccer/blob/main/SECURITY.md#code-scanning
